lessons: A single broad probe from a conflict field (מלחמה, 58 with a rank) located the right field by guess 4, so include one high-yield abstract-social word like war/conflict among the first probes.

After the field was found, the best-ranked words (ניצחון, התקפה) were outcomes and actions of the top word, and the secret was the opposite of the highest scorer (ניצחון), so guess the opposite/outcome of the best-ranked word right after the first rank appears.
Concrete-category probes inside the field (חייל, נשק) scored low (about 25) while abstract event words scored 50-63, so inside a field prefer abstract event/outcome words over objects and people.
Guesses 5-7 and 10-11 (זמן, שלום, חייל, נשק) were spent on side probes that scored below 30; after a rank appears, limit off-field probes to one per batch.

supervisor_log.reason: Early exploration with broad probes needs little thinking; sample semantic dimensions quickly without intensive reasoning.

Player improved best score/rank in the previous round with low effort; still in early exploration phase with only 1 round completed and varied semantic coverage across top guesses, so continued broad probing at low effort is appropriate.
Only 1 round without improvement (threshold is 3+), still in early exploration phase with normal semantic clustering; cluster circling is typically a strategy issue, not a depth issue.
Player just improved (0 rounds since best score increased), still in early exploration phase, and low effort suits broad semantic probing at this stage.

lessons: Broad probes from abstract and social fields located the right field faster than concrete everyday objects (home, water, animals): the first fifteen guesses on concrete objects gave almost nothing, so open with abstract and social fields.

Once a field is found, do not spend dozens of guesses on synonyms and inflections of the same word: when several neighbours plateau at the same score, switch to the outcome, the opposite or the cause of the top-ranked words.
Hebrew construct forms and inflections (construct state, plurals, possessives) score about the same as the base word and waste guesses, so skip them.

Two earlier games stalled for 5 to 8 rounds (the best score unchanged for 25 to 40 guesses) while every guess stayed inside one cluster; after two rounds without a new best, change axis instead of adding more neighbours.
supervisor_lessons: Observation from two earlier games (effort levels were not recorded then): the best similarity stayed unchanged for 5 and 8 consecutive rounds while the player circled one cluster of near-synonyms, so stalls of this length are common.

It is not yet known whether raising effort ends such a stall; the record of effort levels and outcomes starts with the next games, so judge from the effort statistics you are shown, not from assumptions.
In the one earlier game that ended, the plateau broke when the player switched to the outcome side of the concept; effort levels were not recorded, so whether thinking depth mattered is unknown.
A single-round stall during active exploration does not warrant escalation; the player's sub-agents can regroup naturally at low effort, so waiting before raising is justified.

Low effort was not a bottleneck here—the player solved in 4 rounds—suggesting that strategy diversity (switching to a new conceptual axis) can happen without depth increase, so do not conflate strategy stalls with thinking-power gaps.

Committing to low effort when early rounds show alternate successes (improving in rounds 1, 3, and 4) prevents premature escalation; once a strategy proves it can self-correct within 1-2 rounds, trust it rather than raising.
